title: Bhote Koshi 2026
subtitle: Glacier collapse in Tibet to the Chitwan lowland — 26 August 2026
t0Note: USGS seismic signal Ms 5.2 at 02:52 UTC (08:37 Nepal time), reinterpreted as the collapse itself, not a tectonic quake.

path.note: Digitised from known river towns along the Lhende Khola → Bhote Koshi → Trishuli → Narayani course. The app snaps every point to the DEM thalweg (lowest point across the valley) at load, so lateral error in these seeds is corrected against real elevation data.

routing.note: Front speed v = clamp(k·√gradient, 3, 26) m/s with gradient in m/km from the DEM thalweg. k is varied over 1.6–3.0 to produce the arrival-time band. This is a labelled estimate, not a calibrated hydraulic model.

stages.title: Glacier collapse
stages.body: An ice–rock avalanche breaks free at roughly 5,200–5,400 m under clear skies — no rain, no river rise, no earthquake. The seismic signal was the collapse itself.

stages.title: Natural dam forms
stages.body: The debris moves north-west, then west, and slams into the Lhende Khola, temporarily blocking the river with ice, rock and mud.

stages.title: Barrier lake bursts
stages.body: Water backs up behind the blockage, then the dam fails. The released surge sweeps up more ice, water, rock and sediment and amplifies as it descends.

stages.title: Rasuwagadhi
stages.body: The flow strikes the border post. Bridges linking Nepal and Tibet are torn away; Chinese surveillance footage shows a wall of mud engulfing buildings as people run.

stages.title: Timure
stages.body: Customs containers, freight and an EV charging station are swept off the bank. The road north to the border is destroyed.

stages.title: Syabrubesi
stages.body: The main trekking gateway takes direct damage: riverside buildings and the road north are gone. Hydropower infrastructure along the reach is wrecked.

stages.title: Betrawati
stages.body: The debris flow leaves the gorge and merges into the Trishuli. A river gauge here measures water rise — it can register the flood only once it has already arrived.

stages.title: Bidur · Nuwakot
stages.body: The swollen Trishuli races through Nuwakot. Phone video from a bus in Bidur captures the chaos as the river tears through the valley floor.

stages.title: Malekhu · Prithvi Highway
stages.body: The river runs beside the country's main east–west highway. A stretch of the Prithvi Highway is closed, briefly cutting Kathmandu from Pokhara by road.

stages.title: Mugling
stages.body: The Marsyangdi joins and the river turns south toward the Terai. Bodies from upstream are recovered along this reach in the days that follow.

stages.title: Narayanghat · Chitwan
stages.body: Debris and victims are carried as far as the Chitwan lowland, roughly 170 km from the collapse.

warningSites.name: River gauge · Betrawati
warningSites.note: Hydrological station on the Trishuli (location approximate). A gauge detects rising water where it stands — it cannot see a collapse 40 km upstream.

warningSites.name: Joint China–Nepal glacier EWS · Rasuwagadhi area
warningSites.note: A cross-border early-warning system for melting glaciers was reported to exist; whether it fired, and for what, is under review. Systems here watch rain and glacial-lake levels, not sudden clear-sky ice collapses.

witnesses.name: Surveillance video · Chinese side
witnesses.note: Wall of mud and water crashes over a building as people run. Time on footage not yet verified.

witnesses.name: Phone video · bus passenger, Bidur
witnesses.note: Passenger captures the surge from a bus. Time not yet verified.

overlay2025.title: 8 July 2025 — the same channel
overlay2025.body: Thirteen months earlier a supraglacial lake north of Langtang Himal drained into the Lhende Khola and surged down the Bhote Koshi: 9 dead, 20+ missing, the Friendship (Miteri) Bridge destroyed, four hydropower projects damaged. Bodies were recovered as far as Dhading and Chitwan. This was a known-hazard valley.

barrierLake.title: Live risk: barrier lake still upstream
barrierLake.body: On 27 Aug Chinese authorities warned that a ~2,000,000 m³ lake had formed behind the collapse debris, with a high chance of breach given ~3,000,000 m³ of expected inflow. It overflowed slightly on 28 Aug; Rasuwa officials were warned.

toll.note: Figures rose sharply over the first four days and remain provisional; some people may be counted on both sides of the border. Nationals of ~32 countries are among the missing, including Kailash pilgrims and trekkers.
